about: Source of truth for what the daily loop may build. One lane per IST weekday. The loop scores ONLY the pool of the slot's lane plus fresh signal-derived ideas that fit that lane. backlog/backlog.md is the pre-2026-09-24 archive and is not read during daily runs.

lanes.name: Azure & Microsoft AI
lanes.scope: Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Agent Service, AI Search, Content Safety, Entra for AI workloads, Microsoft Agent Framework / Semantic Kernel. The build must model a Microsoft-documented behaviour.

pool.idea: Provisioned throughput with spillover: model a PTU deployment plus its standard spillover target, drive a traffic shape through it, and show cost split and what the PTU's own 429 chart stops showing.
pool.decision: A platform lead deciding whether to buy PTUs, enable spillover, and which dashboard to trust afterwards.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/spillover-traffic-management
https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/provisioned-throughput

verified.fact: Spillover fires on 429 (PTU exhausted), on 400 for long-context requests a PTU cannot take (gpt-4.1 PTU supports <128K), and on 500/503.
Spilled requests are recorded on the standard deployment with IsSpillover=True and are not counted as 429s on the provisioned deployment.
Provisioned requests cost only the hourly PTU charge; spilled requests bill at standard token rates.
Spillover needs a standard deployment in the same resource with a matching data-processing level; non-OpenAI Foundry models (DeepSeek, Llama) do not support it.

pool.idea: Pick a Foundry resource region and a deployment type (Global, Data Zone, Regional x standard, provisioned, batch) and see where prompts are processed versus where data rests, including which combinations do not exist.
pool.decision: An architect choosing a deployment type that satisfies a stated residency requirement.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types
https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure-region-availability

verified.fact: Data Zone deployments process prompts anywhere within the US, EU (Azure EU Data Boundary, may include EFTA) or APAC zone; Microsoft can add regions to a zone without prior notice.
Data at rest stays in the resource's geography for every deployment type; only processing location changes.
Regional (Azure geography) processing is not available for batch deployments.

pool.idea: Load a labelled sample set (or paste your own) and compare Foundry content-filter configurations by category and severity threshold, annotate vs block, and prompt-shield settings: what each blocks, what it misses, what it wrongly blocks.
pool.decision: A product owner choosing filter thresholds before launch, with the false-block cost visible.
groundIn: Microsoft Learn: Foundry content filtering concepts and configurability (verify the current category and severity model at build time)

pool.idea: RAG index sizing for Azure AI Search: documents, chunking, vector dimensions and replicas in, tier and search units out, with the limit that forces each tier jump named.
pool.decision: An architect or budget owner choosing an AI Search tier for a RAG workload.
groundIn: Microsoft Learn: Azure AI Search service limits and vector index size limits (verify current per-tier numbers at build time; prices are editable inputs)

pool.idea: Model what an AI agent's Microsoft Entra identity can reach under delegated versus application permissions, and what changes when a human is or is not in the loop.
pool.decision: A security lead approving an agent's identity design.
groundIn: Microsoft Learn: Microsoft Entra Agent ID and agent identity documentation (verify availability status and permission model at build time)

lanes.name: Controls that don't hold
lanes.scope: The series' strongest thread: a control you believe you have over an AI system, and the precise documented reason it does not hold. News-driven; any vendor.

pool.idea: The model refused: a refusal at turn 1 and compliance deeper in the same session are the same policy, differently situated. Walk a transcript and watch where published work puts the weak band.
pool.decision: A red-team lead deciding which conversation depths the eval suite must cover.
groundIn: Recent multi-turn jailbreak research (verify dates and figures at build time; do not reuse numbers from this file)

pool.idea: Each step passed, the workflow did not: a multi-step agent workflow where the policy violation appears only in the composition.
pool.decision: An AI governance lead deciding whether per-step checks are sufficient.
groundIn: The September 2026 compositional-policy paper cited in the Day 041 rationale

pool.idea: What your assessor could not check: pick an access tier (API only, logits, fine-tuning, weights, training telemetry, internal docs, right to publish) and see which of OpenAI's four named assessment areas it can test in principle. Needs an interaction that is not a matrix.
pool.decision: A board or risk committee judging what a third-party AI assessment actually established.
groundIn: https://openai.com/index/priorities-principles-third-party-assessments/

lanes.name: Azure x AWS x GCP
lanes.scope: The same decision on three clouds, modelled from each provider's own documentation. Azure is always one of the three.

pool.idea: One model family, three clouds: where inference is processed under Azure Global/Data Zone/Regional, Bedrock in-region vs cross-region inference profiles, and Vertex AI regional vs global endpoints.
pool.decision: An enterprise architect choosing a cloud and deployment option for a residency requirement.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types
AWS Bedrock cross-region inference docs (verify profile types at build time)
Google Vertex AI locations and global endpoint docs (verify at build time)

verified.fact: Azure Data Zone processing spans the whole US, EU or APAC zone.

pool.idea: Azure PTU vs Bedrock Provisioned Throughput vs Vertex Provisioned Throughput: commitment unit, term and break-even against on-demand for your own traffic shape. All prices are editable inputs with source and date shown.
pool.decision: A FinOps or platform lead deciding whether and where to commit.
groundIn: Each provider's provisioned-throughput docs and pricing pages (verify units and terms at build time)

pool.idea: Write one policy (denied topics, PII handling, prompt-attack detection, grounding check) and see which clauses Azure AI Content Safety, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and Google's safety tooling can express, and which silently cannot.
pool.decision: A security architect deciding whether a guardrail policy is portable or cloud-bound.
groundIn: Each provider's guardrail/safety configuration docs (verify at build time)

pool.idea: An agent needs a short list of actions. Find the smallest built-in role that grants them on Azure RBAC, AWS managed policies and GCP predefined roles, and show what each over-grants.
pool.decision: A cloud security lead approving agent permissions across three clouds.
groundIn: Published built-in role definitions for each cloud (verify at build time)

pool.idea: Plan an offline inference job across Azure batch, Bedrock batch and Vertex batch: discount, completion window, and which residency options exist for batch at all.
pool.decision: A data lead choosing where to run a large offline scoring job.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure-region-availability
AWS and GCP batch inference docs (verify at build time)

verified.fact: Azure regional (Azure geography) processing is not available for batch deployments.

lanes.name: M365, Copilot & Graph
lanes.scope: Microsoft 365 Copilot readiness and governance, SharePoint/OneDrive oversharing, Purview labels and DLP for AI, Microsoft Graph permissions. The daily reality of an enterprise IT Director.

pool.idea: Restricted SharePoint Search is retiring and Restricted Content Discovery replaces it. Simulate a tenant's sites and users and show what Copilot can still surface under RCD: content a user owns or recently touched, OneDrive (not covered), and sites still propagating.
pool.decision: An IT Director planning a Copilot rollout, deciding what RCD buys during remediation and what it does not.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery
https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-sharepoint-search

verified.fact: Restricted SharePoint Search is retiring: starting July 31, 2026, new enablement is blocked; Microsoft points to Restricted Content Discovery.
RCD does not change permissions; users can still discover content they own or have recently interacted with.
RCD applies only to SharePoint sites, not OneDrive.
For sites with more than 500,000 items an RCD update can take more than a week to be reflected in search and Copilot.

pool.idea: Draft with Copilot from several labelled files and see which sensitivity label the new document inherits, who can open it, and where the label priority order you configured produces a surprising result.
pool.decision: A compliance admin checking label priority order before Copilot drafting goes live.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot
https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/microsoft-365-copilot-architecture-data-protection-auditing

verified.fact: When Copilot creates content from labelled sources, the highest-priority sensitivity label is inherited, with its protection settings; users can override unless labelling is mandatory.
With encryption, the user needs EXTRACT and VIEW usage rights for Copilot to use the content; user-defined label permissions block Copilot agents from reading the file.

pool.idea: Paste the Graph permissions granted to an app registration and see its effective reach: Sites.Selected stops being a boundary the moment a broader permission such as Files.Read.All is also granted. Suggest the least-privilege set.
pool.decision: An identity admin deciding whether to grant admin consent.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-reference
https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/best-practices-graph-permission

verified.fact: Graph permissions are additive; Sites.Selected does not restrict access when broader permissions like Files.Read.All are also granted.

pool.note: The additive-permissions fact is from a Microsoft Q&A accepted answer. Confirm it against the permissions reference before building.

pool.idea: Model sites with inheritance, broken inheritance, 'Everyone except external users', org-wide and Anyone links, and ownerless sites. See which files each persona's Copilot could ground on, ranked by the documented risk signals.
pool.decision: An IT Director choosing which sites to remediate first before Copilot rollout.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/get-ready-copilot-sharepoint-advanced-management

verified.fact: Microsoft lists oversharing risk signals: Anyone/Everyone/org-wide links, large audiences with excessive permissions, broken inheritance, sensitive content with weak protection, unlabelled or public sites, ownerless or inactive sites.

pool.idea: Purview DLP with the Copilot location: which labelled or sensitive items a policy excludes from Copilot grounding, and which interim controls (RCD, DLP, access restriction) overlap or leave a gap.
pool.decision: A security lead layering interim Copilot protections.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/configure-secure-governed-data-foundation-microsoft-365-copilot

verified.fact: Microsoft's Copilot foundation guidance lists RCD and Purview DLP for Copilot as interim protections to exclude sensitive content from Copilot grounding.

lanes.name: India
lanes.scope: Indic languages, DPDP, IndiaAI Mission models, India's digital public infrastructure, and what global AI platforms mean when the user is in India. Replaces the every-14th-day flagship rule: Friday is the flagship lane every week.

pool.idea: A Foundry resource in Central India with a Data Zone deployment is processed anywhere in the APAC data zone, not in India; batch has no regional option at all. Pick an Indian workload and see which deployment types keep processing in-country, next to the DPDP duties that attach.
pool.decision: An Indian CIO or DPO choosing an Azure AI deployment type for regulated data.
groundIn: https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types
https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure-region-availability
DPDP Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025 (verify obligations and dates at build time)

verified.fact: Data Zone deployments can be processed anywhere in the APAC zone, and Microsoft can add regions to a zone without prior notice.
Regional processing is not available for batch deployments.

pool.idea: Trace one data principal's erasure request under India's DPDP Act through a RAG stack (source store, chunk cache, embeddings, summaries, eval sets, logs) and see which copies the request actually reaches.
pool.decision: An Indian DPO or platform lead scoping what a DPDP erasure request has to touch in an AI system.
groundIn: DPDP Act 2023 s12 and DPDP Rules 2025 (verify obligations and commencement dates at build time)
Vendor docs for each store modelled
pool.note: Re-angled 2026-09-24 from controls/deletion-trace after 4 losses on Timeliness. History kept so the carry limit still applies.

pool.idea: Pick an Indian deployment scenario and see which released IndiaAI-backed models can serve it: licence, weight availability, Indic language coverage, residency, and the DPDP duty that attaches.
pool.decision: An Indian enterprise choosing between sovereign and global models.
groundIn: IndiaAI Mission announcements and model cards (verify releases at build time)

pool.idea: What Indic scripts cost in tokens across published tokenizers, in-browser: the same sentence in English, Hindi, Tamil and Bengali, priced side by side.
pool.decision: A product lead budgeting an Indian-language AI feature.
groundIn: Published tokenizer vocabularies loadable in the browser; provider price pages as editable inputs

pool.idea: Client-side quality inspector for Indic machine-translation output: script consistency, code-mix leakage, number/date/currency localisation errors, no reference translation needed.
pool.decision: A localisation lead deciding whether MT output can ship without human review.
groundIn: Unicode script ranges; Indian numbering and date conventions

pool.idea: Hinglish to Devanagari transliteration and normalisation as you type, with the ambiguity cases shown rather than hidden.
pool.decision: A team deciding how to normalise Hinglish input before search or classification.
groundIn: Published transliteration schemes

pool.idea: Rebuild as a browser demo: anomaly patterns on a synthetic UPI-scale transaction stream, with the detection rules and false-positive cost visible.
pool.decision: A fintech risk lead choosing alert thresholds.
groundIn: NPCI public UPI statistics for scale; synthetic data only

pool.idea: Bilingual Hindi/English retrieval over public agri-scheme documents with citations.
pool.decision: n/a until a redistributable corpus exists.
pool.note: Blocked on a redistributable public corpus small enough to ship in the repo.

lanes.name: Director's toolkit
lanes.scope: Tools an IT or AI Director uses to make a call: cost, risk, reliability, evaluation budgets, build-vs-buy. Every number that can change is an editable input with its source.

pool.idea: How many eval cases do you need to detect a regression of X points at confidence Y? Paired vs unpaired, flaky graders, and what your current suite can and cannot detect.
pool.decision: An AI lead setting the eval budget and release gate.
groundIn: Standard power-analysis formulas, cited inline

pool.idea: Composite availability of an AI application (model endpoint, retrieval, app host, fallback) in series and parallel, with published SLAs as editable inputs.
pool.decision: A Director deciding what SLA the business can actually be promised.
groundIn: Each service's published SLA page (editable inputs, dated)

pool.idea: Describe an AI use case and get its EU AI Act risk tier, the obligations that attach and their dates, plus the matching NIST AI RMF functions.
pool.decision: A governance lead triaging an AI use-case intake.
groundIn: EU AI Act text and implementation timeline; NIST AI RMF 1.0

pool.idea: Three-year TCO: M365 Copilot seats vs a custom Azure OpenAI app vs self-hosting an open model, with a sensitivity chart showing which assumption flips the answer.
pool.decision: A CIO choosing how to deliver an internal AI assistant.
groundIn: Vendor price pages as editable, dated inputs

pool.idea: Allocate a shared AI bill (shared key, shared PTU) to teams under showback, proportional, and reserved-plus-burst models, and see how each distorts behaviour.
pool.decision: A FinOps lead picking an internal chargeback model for AI spend.
groundIn: FinOps Foundation allocation guidance
